
```{r}
#| label: load-data
s <- tar_read(all_summary)
tip_thr <- tar_read(tip_thresholds_tab)

tip2 <- tar_read(tip2_tab)
```

## Prior ladder

The ladder places a sequence of priors on the pooled log-OR. The mild-harm and REMAP-CAP-harm rungs are fixed by the protocol; the other three are proposals awaiting confirmation. The REMAP-CAP-harm rung is also run without the REMAP-CAP contrast in the likelihood, because that trial is otherwise counted twice (once in the prior, once in the data).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ladder-spec
s |> filter(group == "ladder", set == "F1", !drop_remap) |>
  transmute(Rung = rung_label[rung], `Prior on log-OR` = prior_text(mu_mean, mu_sd),
            `Prior 95% interval for OR` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", exp(mu_mean - 1.96 * mu_sd), exp(mu_mean + 1.96 * mu_sd)),
            Status = ifelse(rung %in% c("mild_harm", "remap_harm"), "Protocol-fixed", "Proposal")) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ladder-f1
kable(ladder_tbl(filter(s, group == "ladder", set == "F1")), caption = "F1 prior ladder. The last row repeats the REMAP-CAP-harm rung without the REMAP-CAP contrast.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ladder-f1
#| fig-cap: "F1 prior ladder: prior and posterior intervals."
include_graphics(tar_read(fig_ladder_F1))
```

Moving from the reference prior to the skeptical prior raises the posterior median OR from `{r} pv("ladder_reference", "OR_median")` to `{r} pv("ladder_skeptical", "OR_median")` and lowers P(OR<1) from `{r} pv("ladder_reference", "P_OR_lt_1")` to `{r} pv("ladder_skeptical", "P_OR_lt_1")`. The harm-leaning priors have a larger effect: the posterior median is `{r} pv("ladder_mild_harm", "OR_median")` under the mild-harm prior and `{r} pv("ladder_remap_harm", "OR_median")` under the REMAP-CAP-harm prior, with P(OR<1) of `{r} pv("ladder_mild_harm", "P_OR_lt_1")` and `{r} pv("ladder_remap_harm", "P_OR_lt_1")`. Removing the REMAP-CAP row under the REMAP-CAP-harm prior, which avoids counting that trial twice, gives `{r} pv("ladder_remap_harm_noREMAP", "OR_median")` and `{r} pv("ladder_remap_harm_noREMAP", "P_OR_lt_1")`. The posterior median stays below 1 under every prior in the F1 ladder (largest: `{r} pr(max(filter(s, group == "ladder", set == "F1")$OR_median))`), but with the harm-leaning priors the credible interval is wide and the probability of benefit falls to about three in four.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ladder-f2
kable(ladder_tbl(filter(s, group == "ladder", set == "F2")), caption = "F2 (90-day, 3 trials) prior ladder.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ladder-f3
kable(ladder_tbl(filter(s, group == "ladder", set == "F3")), caption = "F3 (broad-severe, 10 trials) prior ladder.")
```

The 90-day set (F2) is much more sensitive to the prior than F1. With only three trials, one of them the REMAP-CAP contrast, the data do not outweigh a harm-leaning prior: under the mild-harm and REMAP-CAP-harm priors its posterior median OR is `{r} pv("ladder_F2_mild_harm", "OR_median")` and `{r} pv("ladder_F2_remap_harm", "OR_median")`, with P(OR<1) of `{r} pv("ladder_F2_mild_harm", "P_OR_lt_1")` and `{r} pv("ladder_F2_remap_harm", "P_OR_lt_1")`, that is close to no effect. The broad-severe set (F3, ten trials) lies between F1 and F2: `{r} pv("ladder_F3_mild_harm", "OR_median")` and `{r} pv("ladder_F3_remap_harm", "OR_median")` under the same two priors. The 90-day mortality result should therefore be read as uncertain rather than as evidence of no benefit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ladder-f2
#| fig-cap: "F2 prior ladder: prior and posterior intervals."
include_graphics(tar_read(fig_ladder_F2))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ladder-f3
#| fig-cap: "F3 prior ladder: prior and posterior intervals."
include_graphics(tar_read(fig_ladder_F3))
```

## Tipping-point analyses (F1)

### One-dimensional sweep

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tip1
tip_thr |>
  transmute(Probability = ifelse(metric == "P_OR_lt_1", "P(OR<1)", "P(OR<0.833)"), Target = target,
            `Prior SD at which the target is reached` = ifelse(is.na(prior_sd_at_crossing), "not reached on the grid",
                                                               sprintf("%.2f", prior_sd_at_crossing))) |>
  kable(caption = "Skeptical prior Normal(0, SD) on the log-OR: the smallest SD at which the posterior probability reaches the target (linear interpolation on a grid of 0.05).")
```

Read the table as follows: the more skeptical the prior (the smaller the SD), the lower the posterior probability. P(OR<1) stays at or above 0.90 for skeptical priors with an SD of about `{r} pr(tip_thr$prior_sd_at_crossing[1])` or wider, and at or above 0.80 for an SD of about `{r} pr(tip_thr$prior_sd_at_crossing[2])` or wider. At the proposed skeptical rung (SD 0.35) it is `{r} pr(tip_tab$P_OR_lt_1[abs(tip_tab$prior_sd - 0.35) < 1e-9])`. `{r} if (is.na(tip_thr$prior_sd_at_crossing[3])) "P(OR<0.833) does not reach 0.90 for any skeptical prior on the grid." else paste0("P(OR<0.833) reaches 0.90 at an SD of about ", pr(tip_thr$prior_sd_at_crossing[3]), ".")`

```{r}
#| label: fig-tip1
#| fig-cap: "Posterior probabilities against the SD of a skeptical N(0, SD) prior on the log-OR."
include_graphics(tar_read(fig_tipping_F1))
```

### Two-dimensional surface

```{r}
#| label: fig-tip2-p
#| fig-cap: "P(OR<1) over prior centre and SD (48 fits)."
include_graphics(tar_read(fig_tip2_P))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tip2-or
#| fig-cap: "Posterior median OR over prior centre and SD."
include_graphics(tar_read(fig_tip2_OR))
```

```{r}
#| label: tip2-numbers
p_benign <- min(tip2$P_OR_lt_1[tip2$centre_or <= 0.9])
p_conf <- max(tip2$P_OR_lt_1[tip2$centre_or >= 1.25 & tip2$prior_sd <= 0.2])
p_wide <- min(tip2$P_OR_lt_1[tip2$prior_sd >= 0.5])
above1 <- tip2[tip2$OR_median > 1, ]
```

In these maps each cell is one fit: the horizontal axis is the centre of the prior (as an OR; values above 1 mean the prior expects harm), the vertical axis its SD (small means confident). For priors centred on benefit or no effect (OR 0.70 to 0.90) P(OR<1) is at least `{r} pr(p_benign)` at every SD. A harm-leaning prior changes the conclusion only when it is also confident: with a centre of 1.25 or more and an SD of 0.2 or less, P(OR<1) is `{r} pr(p_conf)` or lower, whereas with an SD of 0.5 or more it stays at or above `{r} pr(p_wide)` for every centre. The posterior median OR exceeds 1 only for priors centred at `{r} pr(min(above1$centre_or))` or higher with an SD of `{r} pr(max(above1$prior_sd))` or less. In other words, only a prior that is both centred on harm and held with considerable confidence stops the data from pointing toward benefit.
